parties:
Maklis Ali ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
5. We have heard the learned Advocate who argued the case, in extenso taking us through the grounds and the exhibits appended thereto. It is the submission of tho learned Advocate that he has no other remedy available to him because the time for filing an appeal as provided under the Special Powers Act has already expired and the limitation in the instant case under the Special Powers Act being a special law, section 5 of the Limitation Act will not be applicable and the delay would not be condoned and this has been decided by this court in number of cases and therefore the petitioner has no other forum other than this writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution. It has further been contended by the learned Advocate that in the instant case there was an absence of jurisdiction because schedule and non schedule offences have been tried by the special court which is a nullity and showed us some decisions of this court in this regard. He has further submitted that in the instant case the judgment suffers from an error resulting from mis-appreciation of the evidence namely, that though in the First Information Report there was no mention of any rape it has been subsequently added and found to be so without any evidence on record namely, the victim girl was not examined by any doctor nor she was proved to have been raped by the accused which essentially being an ingredient of the offences as under section 4(ga) of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance and section 366 of the Penal Code; the judgment of conviction cannot stand the scrutiny of law. 

 6. We find no substance in the contention of the learned Advocate in this regard. The contention of the learned Advocate that this application under certiorari is maintainable also has no basis. This court will examine matter on certiorari neither as a court of appeal nor as a court of revision but only in its supervisory capacity only to see that the tribunals do not go wrong in law and examines then the jurisdictional error which arises when the court has no jurisdiction at all. If the court had jurisdiction to entertain a matter the court would be competent to decide a matter rightly and even wrongly yet keeping itself within jurisdiction and any misappreciation of evidence or even finding without proper evidence shall not render Tribunal's exercise and consequent judgment without jurisdiction. In the instant case on this point the learned Advocate submitted that the proceeding is a nullity because this trial of non schedule and schedule offences was held in one trial. We find no warrant for such a view also because in the instant case as it is seen from the facts that the prosecution case had been that the victim girl, who is aged about 10/12 years of age, had been taken away by force on the day following 16-5-87 at about 9 PM when the complainant was in the mosque saying his prayer. It is in the FIR that the accused (petitioner) Moklis Ali and two others being armed with deadly weapons entered into the house of the informant and forcibly abducted his sister Shum Bibi who is a minor girl. This fact was informed to him after he returned from the mosque by the women members of the family and it is further the prosecution case that he made search but he could not find his sister and he lodged the First Information Report and the delay was explained because of the search. So it is clear that the FIR would naturally contain the facts that were known to the complainant at the moment. He could not know the fact of rape that was caused later than the FIR. The victim girl appeared in court as a witness and she categorically stated before the court on solemn affirmation that she was raped by the accused many times and also stated in court that for 3/4 months she was kept at different places by the accused and finding an opportunity she just ran away and returned to her home. A women of a different house, who has no relationship with the accused had been taken away by him by force and he kept her confined for about 3/4 months yet it is the case of the petitioner before this court that there is no record of rape when the victim herself states in court that she has been raped. It is true that the FIR and also the charge sheet submitted by the police did not mention section 376 but when the court framed charge it framed correctly a charge under section 376 of the Penal Code and also under section 4(ga) of Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance and the accused were put on trial to answer a charge under those sections which are both schedule offences. So there is no basis for the allegation that schedule and non schedule offences were tried in one trial. In the instant case we found from the order sheet that from the day the complaint was lodged with the police against him he was just missing and he even could not be arrested by the police in spite of warrant of arrest issued by the court and it appears that the prosecution witnesses were not even cross examined by him. He was tried in absentia and the trial in absentia was held after following the procedures as in law. It was published in the newspapers and all attempts were made to make the accused know that he is facing a trial and only thereafter the court came to a conclusion that he is avoiding arrest and avoiding a trial and then only it would start a trial in absentia. All these steps were carefully taken as required in absentia trial and the order sheet of the case recorded all those steps taken, the Gazette notification made to procure his presence but he would not face the trial but chose to remain a fugitive from law and now comes after 2 years of the order of conviction, to set it aside in writ jurisdiction. We do not find the plea of the petitioner explaining his ignorance to be correct and we find that he has no clean hands for any relief in law or in equity. The provision under Article 102 would not be invoked only to bypass limitation and allow a fugitive from justice to a protection of the court though he has now surrendered.
